clue.text: Rickety car oiled by artist who admired 11

definitions.note: 11 across is the French painter Nicolas Poussin; this Romantic painter studied his work

indicators.note: something rickety is shaky and falling apart, so the letters of car oiled are knocked into a new order

parts.note: by as in multiplication, two by three, is the times sign X

explanation.surface: A shaky old car gets an oiling from a painter with a taste for the old masters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rickety' rearranges CAR OILED into DELACROI; 'by' gives X, the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Delacroix was a French Romantic painter who revered Poussin, the subject of 11 across.

clue.text: Spooner's cheeky entrance having very little

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the sounds starting the two words are exchanged

parts.note: cheeky means pert, impudent
an entrance is a door

explanation.surface: A saucy doorway seems to belong to someone who owns almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of PERT DOOR gives the phrase meaning destitute.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone utterly impoverished, so lacking almost everything is its meaning.

clue.text: Cover over most of Scottish county, being sluggish

indicators.note: a cover placed over the county's letters wraps round them, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a cover is a lid

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept from the county

parts.note: Angus is a county in eastern Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone sluggishly draws a blanket over a large stretch of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the county's last letter and 'over' wraps the cover round what is left. The county lies on Scotland's east coast, north of Dundee.
explanation.definitionFit: A languid person moves slowly and without energy, a close synonym of sluggish.

clue.text: Things to settle about moving up blisters

indicators.note: in a down answer moving up sends a letter higher, towards the start of the word

parts.note: old scores are grudges one has to settle
about is C, short for the Latin circa

explanation.surface: Someone with grudges to settle finds blisters coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving up' lifts C (about) from inside OLD SCORES to the top of the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small viral blisters around the lips, so the plural noun matches blisters.

clue.text: Soliciting without beginning trip

indicators.note: without beginning means the first letter of the word for soliciting is dropped

parts.note: touting is soliciting custom, as a tout does

explanation.surface: A trip spoilt by someone pestering passers-by for business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without beginning' removes the T from TOUTING.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short excursion or jaunt, the same as a trip.

clue.text: Cross, raving about Mark's seasonal greeting

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

indicators.note: about means the word for raving goes round the word for mark

parts.note: raving means mad
a mark on the skin is a scar

explanation.surface: Someone cross and ranting about the festive card a man called Mark sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' looks like a man's name in the possessive; it is a blemish, and 'about' wraps the raving round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A card sent at Christmas carries the season's greetings, so it is a seasonal greeting.

clue.text: Betrays reversal for Bones

indicators.note: reversal means the letters for the betrayal phrase are read backwards

parts.note: one who betrays is rat, a traitor, giving IS RAT

explanation.surface: A double-cross undone, all for the sake of some bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betrays' is taken as IS RAT, a person being a rat; 'reversal' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the small bones of the ankle and foot in anatomy, so they are bones.

clue.text: Best street maps of a dark yellow colour

parts.note: the best is the top
the A-Z is the well-known London street atlas

explanation.surface: The finest street atlases come bound in dark yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a British street atlas, originally of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The gemstone gives its name to a golden brownish-yellow shade.

clue.text: Perhaps Oliver drank gin cocktail, but was in total control

indicators.note: drank means the cocktail goes inside the actor, as a drink would

parts.note: Oliver Reed was a hard-drinking English actor; perhaps flags him as one example of the surname

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: A famously boozy actor downs a gin cocktail yet stays fully in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes the spirit's three letters into IGN, and 'drank' sets them inside the actor's surname. Oliver Reed was notorious for his drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who reigned ruled, holding supreme authority over a realm.

clue.text: Singer put off artist who admired 11

definitions.note: 11 across is the painter Poussin, a model for this neoclassical painter

indicators.note: put off here means put out of order, so the word singer is rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer is put off by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' rearranges SINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres, French neoclassical painter, took Poussin, the subject of 11 across, as a model.

clue.text: Starters in restaurant extremely nasty, annoying lovers of kidneys

indicators.note: starters are opening courses, here the opening letters of the following five words

explanation.surface: Restaurant starters so awful they upset diners who love kidney dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters in' takes the initials of the five words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is the medical term relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: Supply inapt rigs for tediously walking around

indicators.note: read as supple-y, in a supple way, so the letters bend into a new shape

explanation.surface: Providing unsuitable rigs for trudging around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is read as an adverb from supple, not a verb, and rearranges INAPT RIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge wearily from place to place.

clue.text: Chicken cooked in soups

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared afresh, so in soups is rearranged

explanation.surface: A chicken simmered in soups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges IN SOUPS. The word is also the French painter all the artist clues refer to.
explanation.definitionFit: This French culinary term means a very young chicken for roasting.

clue.text: Artist who admired 11 according to old queen on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: according to someone is what that person says, and Anne was Queen of Great Britain in the early 1700s

explanation.surface: Someone announces an artist's admiration on air, citing a long-dead queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the radio' signals a sound-alike: SAYS ANNE is said like the painter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Cézanne, the French Post-Impressionist, said he wanted to redo Poussin from nature.

clue.text: Requests some fabulous red roses from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue from the east means read right to left
some means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Asking for some gorgeous red roses imported from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds SREDRO inside 'fabulous red roses'; 'from the east' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Orders are commands or requests for goods, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Globe reflecting church containing poster for expensive fabric

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the word for globe is read backwards

parts.note: an orb is a globe

indicators.note: containing means the church holds the poster inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a poster is an advert, an AD

explanation.surface: A globe reflected in a church hung with posters for luxurious cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' reads the globe backwards and 'containing' puts the advert inside the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rich woven fabric with a raised pattern, often in gold or silver thread.

clue.text: 25 husks on small island

definitions.note: the solution to 25 down is used here as a noun meaning a bird

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so the husks come first

parts.note: chaff is the husks separated from grain
an inch is a small island in Scottish place names

explanation.surface: Grain husks scattered over a little island.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm. The cross-reference points to 25 down, whose answer means birdlike, here taken as a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This finch is a common European songbird, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Poison stunted the leek?

indicators.note: stunted means cut short, so the last letter of the word the is lost

parts.note: the leek belongs to the plant genus Allium, with onions and garlic

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a poisoned leek is why it never grew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunted' cuts THE to TH; Allium is the leek's genus.
explanation.definitionFit: This toxic metallic element was once used in rat poison and is notorious in murders.

clue.text: Lived under pressure of having occupied chair

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece under another comes below it, so the pressure letter sits on top

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
to have resided is to have lived somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone who lived under the strain of having sat as chairman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the piece placed under comes after, so P comes before RESIDED.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to act as chair of a meeting, so presided matches having been in the chair.

clue.text: Trashy equipment finally makes electric toothbrush handy

parts.note: kit is equipment

indicators.note: finally means the final letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: Tacky gear, but in the end a power toothbrush comes in handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letters of makes, electric, toothbrush, handy: SCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is gaudy, tasteless art or ornament, so the adjective means trashy.

clue.text: Setter's fruit something to do with Trump?

parts.note: the setter is I, and setter's is I am, written I'M
a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: The setter wonders whether their fruit has anything to do with Donald Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' is the setter saying I'M, I am, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The US House voted twice to charge President Trump, so this verb was something done to him.

clue.text: Judge, according to Stone

parts.note: as per means according to

explanation.surface: A judge, as reported by someone named Stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' looks like a surname being quoted; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This opaque variety of quartz, usually red or brown, is a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Cop is as befuddled as artist who admired 11

definitions.note: 11 across is Poussin, whom this Spanish painter admired

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the letters of cop is as are jumbled

explanation.surface: A policeman as baffled as a modern painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'befuddled' rearranges COP IS AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso, the Spanish painter, admired Poussin and painted a version of his Bacchanal.

clue.text: Confused bear has question for artist who admired 11

indicators.note: has means holds, so the question abbreviation is held inside
confused means muddled, so the letters of bear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled bear puts a question to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' turns the animal into BRAE, and 'has' holds the question abbreviation in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Braque, French co-founder of Cubism, admired Poussin, the subject of 11 across.

clue.text: Regrets getting up next to artist who admired 11

indicators.note: in a down answer getting up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so regrets is rues
at can mean next to or beside, as in at the door

explanation.surface: Someone with regrets rises beside a painter who loved Poussin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' reverses the regrets into SEUR, as a down answer is read upwards. 'next to' is not a placement signal here but a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Seurat, the French pointillist, admired Poussin's ordered classical compositions.

clue.text: Royal Academy help a struggling artist who influenced 11

definitions.note: 11 across is Poussin, who drew heavily on this Renaissance master

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy of Arts in London

indicators.note: struggling means floundering, so the letters of help a are thrown about

explanation.surface: The Royal Academy lends a hand to a painter who is having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges HELP A into PHAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian Renaissance painter Raphael was a major influence on Poussin's classical style.

clue.text: One going through Norway like a bird

parts.note: one is the article a
via means going by way of, through
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Someone travelling via Norway, flying like a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going through' looks like an insertion signal but simply gives VIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or resembling birds.

clue.text: Swears about shocking treatment of possessions

indicators.note: about means the swear words go round the treatment

parts.note: to eff is to swear, so effs is swears
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, electric shock treatment

explanation.surface: Someone curses over shock therapy given to possessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the swearing round the therapy. To eff is British slang for to swear, from the F-word.
explanation.definitionFit: One's personal effects are one's belongings.

clue.text: QI failure amazingly the one through to the next round

definitions.text: the one through to the next round

indicators.note: amazingly suggests something turned upside down, so the letters of QI failure are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flop on the quiz show QI, yet somehow it makes the next round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazingly' rearranges QI FAILURE. QI is a BBC panel quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: In a competition, a qualifier is a contestant who has earned a place in a later stage.

clue.text: I don't agree with that Sun journalist getting investigated

parts.note: a flat refusal of agreement is no
S is short for Sunday or sun
ED is an editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A tabloid reporter from the Sun objects after being probed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' suggests the British tabloid newspaper but simply gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose around is to pry or snoop, so nosed means poked into or investigated.

clue.text: Hunt for Cruise, then a replacement

indicators.note: a replacement means letters put back in other places, so then a is rearranged

explanation.surface: A search for a cruise ship, then one to replace it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' and 'Cruise' look like a search and a holiday; they are the Mission: Impossible hero and Tom Cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Cruise plays the spy Ethan Hunt in the Mission: Impossible films, so this first name is his role's.

clue.text: Splinters tie court down

parts.note: a tie is a match, a fixture between teams
to court is to woo

explanation.surface: Splinters fly as a game draw gets a tennis court shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' and 'court' suggest sport but give MATCH and WOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means wood reduced to splinters or tiny fragments.
